module.name: WRSADC

modules_linked: Scaffolding.md ↔ TFT_Primitives.md — architectural rationale ↔ operator specification

primitive_1.role: Foundational awareness — raw input becomes patterned position

primitive_2.label: Act → Adjust → Align
primitive_2.role: Behavioral arc — position becomes calibrated action

primitive_3.label: Reflect → Refine → Reinforce
primitive_3.role: Consolidation loop — action becomes durable learning

rtt-core (resonance-aware structural grammar, dimensional tracking concepts)

files.purpose: Module front door — AI-Ready badge, purpose statement, two-implementation overview (Python core + shell logger), integration summary.

Architectural rationale document — explains why WRSADC belongs in TFT_3Pack, defines insertion point in repo tree, specifies minimal feature set (dimensional tracking, state transitions, structural snapshots, debug introspection).

Full specification of all three triadic primitives with WRSADC integration — Python and shell examples, micro-phase definitions, structural pairing rationale (perceive↔record, interpret↔map, orient↔summarize).
Python package initializer — imports WRSADC class from wrsadc_core and exports it as the public API surface.
Core dimensional engine — WRSADCEvent and WRSADCSnapshot dataclasses, WRSADC class with observe() for state logging, snapshot() for structural summaries, debug_print() for triadic introspection.
Shell adapter — wrsadc_init() sets context, wrsadc_mark() appends timestamped events to log file, wrsadc_summary() aggregates dimensions and states from log.
Python implementation of Primitive 1 (Perceive → Interpret → Orient) with WRSADC observe() hooks at each micro-phase transition.
Shell implementation of Primitive 1 (Perceive → Interpret → Orient) sourcing wrsadc_shell.sh and calling wrsadc_mark at each micro-phase.
Python implementation of Primitive 2 (Act → Adjust → Align) — behavioral arc with WRSADC observe() hooks.
Python implementation of Primitive 3 (Reflect → Refine → Reinforce) — consolidation loop with WRSADC observe() hooks.
